messages:
deploy-bot: Started canary rollout v2.14 -> 10% of inference pods in us-west-2 :rocket:

dave.eng: heads-up, I see a few of the canary pods in CrashLoopBackOff already. attaching logs in a sec

alice.sre: paging oncall, crashloops on canary at ~10% after deploy, sounds like termination handling issue :rotating_light:

incident-bot: @carol.oncall you have been paged for channel incidents (priority: high) — reason: canary pods crashlooping after deploy

carol.oncall: I'm on it. pulling logs now. any customer reports?

ben.dev: Not yet in Sentry but our synthetic inference checks in prod-us-west show 5% 500s and 30% latency tail spike for short requests

alice.sre: kube describe on one of the pods:
```
Name:         inf-ff-canary-5b7f9
State:        Waiting
  Reason:     CrashLoopBackOff
Last Termination: ExitCode=143 (SIGTERM)
Events:
  Warning  Unhealthy  Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503
  Normal   Killing    Stopping container with SIGTERM
```
Looks like SIGTERM + liveness failing during shutdown. readiness probe timing maybe too aggressive.

ben.dev: We rolled a small change to gracefulShutdown timeout in app-runtime yesterday, might be related. The liveness/readiness probes are pretty tight: initialDelaySeconds: 5, periodSeconds: 5

carol.oncall: HPA shows scale-down triggering right when the pods are terminating, I think drain plus probe -> SIGTERM chain. HPA minReplicas is 1 but target CPU is low so it scaled down the older replicas as new ones rolled, creating brief 0->1 situations?

alice.sre: Can you paste the hpa and deployment spec?

ben.dev: quick snippet:
```
spec:
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 50
---
readinessProbe:
  httpGet: /health
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 5
livenessProbe:
  httpGet: /healthz
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 5
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 20
```
this matches what we shipped.

alice.sre: seems likely the new image increases shutdown time (in-flight KV flush). terminationGracePeriodSeconds 20 is too short. plus probes are too aggressive for this version.

carol.oncall: Impact: synthetic checks failing in us-west, some dedicated customer routes hit 503s intermittently — not widespread but definitely customer visible. I flagged severity: sev2.

dave.eng: We should hit the kill-switch for the feature flag to stop routing traffic to canaries and then rollback the deployment. I can flip the flag now.

ben.dev: flipping feature flag: ff_canary_v2 -> OFF :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Canary routing disabled for ff_canary_v2. No new traffic will be sent to canary pods.

carol.oncall: Ok traffic stopped, but pods are still crashlooping and HPA is oscillating. Recommend rollback to v2.13 which was stable.

alice.sre: Agreed. @dave.eng please start rollback job. I'll watch for node evictions and HPA activity.

dave.eng: Kicking a rollback to image v2.13 now:
```
kubectl set image deployment/inference inference=registry/redwood/inference:v2.13 -n prod
```

incident-bot: Rollback job started by dave.eng (deployment inference -> v2.13)

dave.eng: Rollback applied. kubectl rollout status shows: "deployment \"inference\" successfully rolled out"

ben.dev: Confirming older pods stable, no new crashloops observed after rollout.

carol.oncall: Synthetics show 500s down to baseline, tail latencies improving. Customer-facing errors cleared for affected tenants.

alice.sre: HPA settled back to normal. No node drain events correlated during rollback window. Looking at logs, the v2.14 image sent SIGTERM later (longer pre-stop) which combined with tight probes led to liveness kills.

dave.eng: We'll push a hotfix branch to increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds and relax probes for a canary-specific deployment before re-attempting. Also add a pre-deploy test that runs graceful shutdown integration.

carol.oncall: Notifying CSM and support with impact summary: ~3% of requests in us-west saw 500s for ~12 minutes during canary rollout, no data loss, customers auto-recovered, workaround was rollback/kill-switch.

alice.sre: Assigning postmortem owners: ben.dev (root cause), dave.eng (deploy process), alice.sre (mitigations + runbook updates). We'll schedule 60m postmortem within 48h.

ben.dev: quick actions I will take: increase terminationGracePeriodSeconds -> 60, initialDelaySeconds -> 10 for readiness/liveness on canary, add CI shutdown test, and gate canary at 0 traffic until health checks stable.

dave.eng: I'll create a rollback-runbook PR and add a deploy-bot validation to check probes vs terminationGracePeriodSeconds delta.

carol.oncall: Closing incident channel when runbook PR is merged. Thanks all. :tada:

alice.sre: Marking incident as resolved in the channel. Follow-up: postmortem template link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/pm-XXXX

incident-bot: Incident resolved by carol.oncall — severity downgraded to sev3 after rollback and mitigation. Postmortem assigned.
